item.title: Customs hands over seized LPG laden truck to NMDPRA in Calabar
item.description: …auctions seized PMS worth N6.1million By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Customs Service, through Operation Whirlwind, on Friday handed over an intercepted truck conveying diverted Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). The truck, with registration number KAM 663 XA, was handed over at the Customs House, Calabar. It was intercepted by operatives of the Operation Whirlwind Zone C team, Calabar Axis. The National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, Drputy Comptroller of Cutsoms , Mahmood Bello Esq , performed the handover on the directive of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi. Bello said the handover demonstrated the importance of cooperation between government agencies. “The formal handover to NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency cooperation in ensuring appropriate regulatory action and accountability,” he said. He described the diversion and smuggling of petroleum products as a threat to the country’s economy . “The illegal diversion and smuggling of petroleum products remain serious threats to our national economy, energy security and public interest,” he said. Speaking earlier , the Acting Customs Area Controller, Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, Nkiruka Nwalla said the exercise showed the Service’s resolve to enforce petroleum regulations. “The formal handover of this LPG tanker to the NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency collaboration in ensuring regulatory compliance and accountability in the petroleum sector,” she said. The Service also publicly auctioned 6,125 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), packed in 245 jerrycans of 25 litres each. The fuel was seized at Ikang Road (Bakassi), Ibaka and Mfum. Its Duty Paid Value is N6,125,000. Bello said the auction followed established procedures and was meant to ensure transparency, particularly because seized petroleum products are volatile and must be disposed of promptly. Bello said intelligence reports indicated that attempts to divert and smuggle PMS and other products could increase during the festive season. He directed all commanders to raise operational readiness and strengthen surveillance around known flashpoints. He also said Operation Whirlwind would not stop at seizures adding that they must identify offenders and prosecute them. “Our mandate goes beyond making seizures; we must ensure that identified offenders are properly investigated and prosecuted,” he said. Bello, the newly appointed National Coordinator, pledged purposeful leadership and a more intelligence-driven approach. “We will ensure that economic saboteurs find no refuge anywhere within our operational environment,” he added. item.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. Now we have just one more match to win, and we’re determined to make history.” Nigeria

item.title: ‎APC explains omission of ex-Jigawa governor Badaru from campaign council
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, DUTSE ‎The All Progressives Congress, APC, in Jigawa State has explained why former governor and ex-Minister of Defence, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, was not included in the party’s recently-announced governorship campaign council. Jigawa State House of Assembly’ Speaker, Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, gave the explanation while responding to questions from journalists over Badaru’s absence from the list. ‎Dangyatin said Badaru, being a prominent national political figure, has broader responsibilities at the national level ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎According to him, assigning the former governor to the state governorship campaign council would limit his ability to contribute to the party’s campaign efforts at the national and regional levels. ‎“Including the former governor in the governorship campaign council is like tying him down and restricting him from contributing to the party’s victory,” the Speaker said. ‎He added that Badaru currently serves as the Director-General of Arewa for Asiwaju, a position that requires him to coordinate political activities across the North and the country. ‎“The former governor is the Director-General of Arewa for Asiwaju. He is dealing with the entire region and the country,” Dangyatin stated. ‎The Speaker, however, dismissed speculations that Badaru’s exclusion from the campaign council was connected to internal divisions within the Jigawa APC. ‎He maintained that the party had no disagreement with the former governor, insisting that the APC in the state remained united. ‎Dangyatin urged party supporters to disregard what he described as rumours and propaganda surrounding Badaru’s omission and instead focus on mobilising support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Troops rescue three female kidnap victims in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, JOS Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have rescued three female kidnap victims unharmed after confronting their abductors at Makundang village, Mangor District, in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victims were rescued following a search-and-rescue operation launched by troops of Sector 5 of OPEP after receiving a distress report about a kidnapping incident at about 8:50 p.m. on November 5, 2026. Security sources told newsmen that the troops swiftly mobilised to the area and established contact with the kidnappers, who reportedly abandoned their victims and fled into the surrounding bush following pressure from the security personnel. The rescued victims were identified as Miss Fatigi Aguna, 19; Lovina Bawa, 18; and Barsheba Appolos, 18. The sources said all three victims were rescued unhurt and subsequently reunited with their families. They added that troops had intensified efforts to track down and apprehend the fleeing kidnappers, assuring residents that security operations were ongoing to prevent further criminal activities in the area. Confirming the development on Saturday, the spokesperson for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, said the operation was part of ongoing efforts by security personnel to protect lives and property across the Joint Operations Area. Oteh appreciated residents for their cooperation with security agencies and appealed for sustained support through the provision of credible and timely information to assist security operatives in restoring lasting peace in the area. He urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to security agencies, noting that public cooperation remained vital to the success of ongoing operations. item.title: 2027: Why is Obi facing attacks despite finishing third in 2023? – Utomi
item.description: Professor of Political Economy, Pat Utomi, has questioned the criticism directed at former Anambra State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, asking why he continues to face attacks despite finishing third in the 2023 presidential election. Utomi raised the question in a post on his verified X handle on Saturday, saying the level of hostility towards Obi deserved an explanation. “There is no convincing explanation for why a candidate who finished third in the 2023 presidential election attracts this level of hostility from all directions. “The intensity of the attacks raises questions that Nigerians deserve answers to. Perhaps one day, we will finally understand what really happened in 2023,” Utomi wrote. Although Utomi did not mention any individual or political party in his post, his comments came after criticism from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his vice, Kashim Shettima, including the senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole. Recall that Tinubu took a swipe at Obi at the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally held at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on Friday, accusing the former Anambra governor of failing to tackle erosion during his time in office while contrasting it with his own record as Lagos State governor. “He’s in one party; they called NDC, who is running for president; he ran away from erosion in Anambra State. He could not confront erosion,” Tinubu said. “I, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, confronted the Atlantic Ocean; I tamed it for you. Umo Eno confronted the erosion in Akwa Ibom, and it’s working for you.” Similarly, Shettima at the same event accused Obi of losing the goodwill he previously enjoyed among Nigerians, alleging that the NDC candidate had relied on false claims and misleading statistics. “And clearly this gentle man has run himself out of this race with his lies and bogus statistics. We warned him that he’ll get to that. “Peter Obi has clearly messed up and squandered away his goodwill; he no longer excites when he speaks these days. He draws suspicions; it’s too bad for him.” Oshiomhole, during an appearance on Channels TV Politics Today on Thursday, described the Obi as a trader who has failed to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies ahead of the 2027 general election. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security. What will you do differently? He said it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short-term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. item.title: Naira Would Have Been Worthless Without Economic Reforms, Tinubu Tells Nigerians
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has defended his administration’s economic reforms, saying the naira would have become worthless if his government had failed to take decisive action to remove the fuel subsidy upon assuming office. He made the remarks at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium. Tinubu said his administration inherited an economy in which 27 of the country’s 36 state governors were unable to meet their salary obligations, let alone pay pensions and gratuities. “When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary obligation, not to talk of pension and gratuity. Today I stand before you able to say we are out of that tunnel. I can beat my chest to say we are out of the greatest despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of possible bankruptcy.” Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026. Defending the decisions taken by his government, the President said: “By now, if we didn’t take a decision, the day I took over, we would use wheelbarrows to move our naira. Because it would have been valueless, nothing.” He added that the exchange rate was about ₦1,300 to the dollar, arguing that the currency had retained some value because of the decisions his administration took. President Tinubu insisted that his administration would not reverse its decision to end the policy. Using the biblical account of Moses and the Israelites’ departure from Egypt, he said Nigeria must continue moving forward, stating: “Nigeria will never go back to the subsidy.” “We are talking of $1,300 now to a dollar. Because it still has pocketable value. If we had left it, it would have been a wheelbarrow when you go to a tomato market. That is the truth.” Tinubu also aimed at opposition figures Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar, questioning their leadership capacity and accusing them of abandoning difficult situations. He criticised Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), over the erosion challenges in Anambra State, while accusing Atiku, now the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, of abandoning the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) when his leadership came under challenge. item.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
item.description: Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme. Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States. He also said Iran’s forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday. “Today, the Islamic Republic’s armed forces… having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war,” he said. “They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence.” “Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations,” he added. – Reward offered – On Friday, the US military said it was offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme. Rewards for Justice, a State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including “facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X. The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests. In a statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.” It did not specify what type of information would warrant a $20 million reward. US President Donald Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear programme. “If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. “If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.” – Dialogue – The president also said Iran — which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war — is eager to end the conflict. “We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said. Trump called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on Friday to discuss efforts to end the war. item.title: Police detain officer over fatal shooting of young girl in Lagos
item.description: By Matthew Johnson The Lagos state police command has disarmed and detained Assistant Superintendent of Police, ASP Omotayo Olajide, following the fatal shooting of a young girl, Omole Taiwo, and the injury of another in the Nosamu area of Ajegunle. The tragic incident occurred on Thursday night, November 5, 2026, between 9:30 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., when police operatives were deployed to the area to quell a violent clash over toll collection between two rival groups known as the Nosamu Boys and the Alayabiagba Boys. According to a statement issued on Saturday by the Command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Abimbola Adebisi, the rival factions were reportedly armed with cutlasses and other dangerous weapons. She said during the operation to restore order, ASP Olajide discharged his firearm, and the bullet struck the two girls. She said both victims were rushed to the Ajeromi General Hospital for emergency treatment. Taiwo was later transferred to the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH) in Ikeja, where she was pronounced dead. The second child remains hospitalised and is reported to be in stable condition. She said the command expressed deep sorrow over the loss of an innocent life and confirmed that the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for a thorough and impartial inquiry. She explained that the investigation aims to establish the exact circumstances surrounding the shooting and determine the appropriate legal and disciplinary measures. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Tijani Fatai, has visited the bereaved family to offer his condolences. He assured them that justice would be served and pledged that no officer found culpable would be shielded. Reaffirming the Command’s commitment to transparency, accountability, and the protection of human life, the police urged anyone with information that could assist the investigation to report to the nearest police station or the Command’s Public Relations Department. item.title: Paraguay Senate impeaches President Peña, VP Alliana takes over
item.description: Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay on Friday following the impeachment of his predecessor over a massive banking crisis that locked almost half the country out of their accounts. Senators appointed Alliana, the former vice president, shortly after voting to remove Santiago Pena over the chaotic collapse of a bank to which he had links. Senate President Basilio Nunez declared Pena “guilty of poor performance in his duties” after 44 out of 45 senators voted in favor of impeachment, with one lawmaker absent. Hundreds of people waiting outside Congress raucously celebrated his impeachment. “Justice has been done. Now we want him to give us back our money and go to jail,” Jessica Aquino, 32, told AFP. Paraguayan authorities placed the ex-leader under house arrest minutes after his removal, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester told reporters. Alliana promised not to abandon the almost three million depositors, including pensioners, affected by Ueno Bank’s takeover amid insolvency concerns. “Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated,” said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028. Opposition lawmakers had also filed a motion to impeach Alliana over the crisis, but the request failed to gain congressional approval. – Money trickles back – The bank’s demise brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno. Advance payments to an unspecified number of impacted depositors began on Thursday afternoon, a Central Bank official told AFP. The first phase of aid deposits, up to around $1,600, will go to clients who don’t have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, said Jose Maciel of the Central Bank’s Deposit Guarantee Fund. The next beneficiaries “will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process,” he added. Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that have stripped him of political immunity. The opposition accused the US-backed politician of a conflict of interest, which he denied. The Attorney General said it was investigating him for “acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity.” He will be questioned over alleged crimes of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds on Saturday, prosecutor Gonzalez Vester said. Pena urged reconciliation in an X post shortly before his removal. “Today, we must come together as Paraguayans to rebuild our institutions and restore trust,” he said. item.title: Houston mayor limits immigration agents cooperation by police after Democratic victory
item.description: The mayor of Houston, Texas announced Friday that the city’s police department will limit its cooperation with federal immigration agents after Democrats swept midterm elections this week. The so-called “blue tsunami” ousted Republican Governor Greg Abbott, a close Texas ally of US President Donald Trump, who has cracked down on immigration with raids conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents since returning to office last year. Abbott had threatened in April to revoke $110 million in public safety funding from Houston if city officials didn’t walk back a similar measure earlier this year, and city officials complied. He lost reelection on Tuesday and will be replaced by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, the first Latina woman elected governor of Texas. Now, Houston Mayor John Whitmire has signed an executive order instructing Houston police to not contact ICE agents when a person is detained for nonviolent offenses, like a traffic stop. “It’s to reduce the fear and anxiety, not just in some of our communities but across Houston,” Whitmire said during a press conference announcing the change. The 77-year-old mayor acknowledged that the change could bring some political risks but said he was ready to meet them, as Abbott and other Republicans remain in power until January. ICE released a statement on X reacting to the change, writing: “Watching child porn and selling heroin are classified as ‘nonviolent offenses’ by the way.” “This is the Mayor of Houston directly advocating for policies that protect some of the worst criminals in America,” it added. According to the Prison Policy Initiative, a nonpartisan think tank, Texas has had more arrests carried out by ICE agents during Trump’s second term than any other state, with almost 137,000 recorded as of August 2026. Texas is also the state with the highest number of ICE detainees in the US, with over 16,000 held at various facilities — more than double the amount held in the second highest state, Louisiana — according to Syracuse University’s Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. item.title: How pregnant woman delivered inside Danfo in Lagos
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Passengers inside a commercial bus, popularly called Danfo in Lagos were stunned when a fellow passenger suddenly went into sudden labor and successfully gave birth to a baby boy on board. According to Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the woman was traveling across the state when labor began unexpectedly mid-journey In the process, fellow commuters and onlookers quickly assisted her through the delivery inside the vehicle while others went into prayer session for safe delivery. Medical responders and local commuters assisted in securing the mother and child immediately following the emergency delivery. Fortunately, after few minutes, the baby boy was delivered safely. In viral footage capturing the moments following the birth, witnesses suggested naming the child Abiona—a traditional Yoruba name commonly associated with a child born on a journey or along the road. Recall that a similar incident happened at Onipanu Bus Stop, along Ikorodu Road sometimes ago. “In a swift r​esponse, LASEMA arrived at the scene to assist a pregnant woman who went into sudden labor while waiting for transport. “The woman delivered a healthy baby boy. Both mother and child were stabilized by LASEMA paramedics before being transported to a nearby healthcare facility for post-natal care,” LASEMA Permanent Secretary, Dr. Femi Oke-Osanyintolu stated. item.title: The Records Are On The Ballot
item.description: The campaign has acquired a sharper edge: In Akwa Ibom Today, President Bola Tinubu challenged the leadership credentials of his principal opponents. His apparent references to Peter Obi’s handling of erosion in Anambra and Atiku Abubakar’s departure from the PDP sought to turn their past decisions into questions about their fitness to govern. These were campaign accusations, rather than independently established assessments of their records. Vice-President Kashim Shettima reinforced the attack, questioning Obi’s credibility and arguing that Atiku’s experience should be judged by accomplishments rather than years in office. His assertion that Obi has lost goodwill remains a partisan assessment; it does not establish a measurable change in voter support. The political intention is clear: put the challengers on the defensive. That matters for an incumbent whose own performance is under examination. If voters spend more time debating whether the opposition is credible, the government gains room to argue that continuity is the safer choice. But scrutiny travels both ways. Once the campaign becomes a comparison of records, Tinubu must also answer for the results of his presidency: purchasing power, security, employment and public services. UYO: Projects and Political Persuasion Today’s visit combined the inauguration of projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration with a political gathering. It gave Tinubu a setting in which visible infrastructure and electoral advocacy could reinforce each other. The distinction between state projects and federal achievements still matters. Political cooperation can support delivery, but credit should follow the evidence about funding, execution and responsibility. For the governing camp, the opportunity is to connect infrastructure with an argument about competent government. For voters, the question is how those investments improve transport, commerce, services and livelihoods. An inauguration provides a powerful picture. Its electoral value depends on the public’s experience after the ceremony. ATIKU: Defiance Needs a Legal Foundation Atiku’s response today remained combative. In a statement, he accused the government of using the courts to evade electoral judgment and reaffirmed his intention to challenge the ruling. That allegation requires attribution; it is not proof of government direction of the proceedings. His campaign also continued in Kebbi on Thursday, despite the judgment. Reporting published today describes promises on security, employment and restoring fuel subsidies. The event should therefore be treated as yesterday’s campaign activity, rather than a fresh Friday rally. Politically, continuing to campaign signals resolve. Legally, public assurances cannot settle the status of a nomination. The subsidy proposal also deserves close questioning. What would be subsidised? Who would benefit? item.title: Nigeria Presides Over Key UN Election
item.description: Nigeria has presided over key elections at the United Nations General Assembly’s Fifth Committee, with Mauritania and Israel emerging as beneficiaries of two significant appointments during the 81st Session of the General Assembly. The elections, conducted under the chairmanship of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, saw C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania recommended as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission, while Israel’s candidate, Shai Mazai, secured a place on the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. In a demonstration of transparency in the electoral process, Ambassador Ibrahim directed that the ballot boxes be opened before voting commenced, allowing delegates to verify the boxes ahead of the collection of ballots. In the contest for the chairmanship of the International Civil Service Commission, C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania secured 102 votes, defeating Mrs. Maria of Zimbabwe, who polled 82 votes. Having obtained the required majority of 93 votes, Mohammed was recommended by the Fifth Committee to the General Assembly for designation as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission for a four-year term beginning January 1, 2027. In another significant outcome, Israel’s Mr. Shai Mazai secured 134 votes to emerge as the recommended candidate from the Group of Western European and Other States to the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee subsequently recommended his appointment to the committee for a three-year term, also beginning January 1, 2027. The elections formed part of the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119, which covers appointments to fill vacancies in subsidiary organs and other appointments. Other bodies considered during the exercise included the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, the Committee on Contributions and the Investment Committee, alongside the International Civil Service Commission and the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee, chaired by Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, also recommended candidates from other regional groups to the International Civil Service Commission through acclamation, following the absence of contested nominations for the respective seats. At the conclusion of the exercise, Ambassador Ibrahim commended delegates for their patience, cooperation and commitment throughout the electoral process. He also congratulated those recommended for appointment and urged them to uphold the integrity of the Fifth Committee while discharging their responsibilities. The Nigerian diplomat equally acknowledged the contributions of the tellers and officials nominated by Member States to supervise the electoral process. Ambassador Ibrahim subsequently declared the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119 concluded and requested the Rapporteur to communicate its decisions to the General Assembly for further action. item.title: 2027: Opposition’s battle for space
item.description: Within a span of one week, opposition political parties in Nigeria have experienced various challenges in their bid to contest in the 2027 general elections. From the bids for the presidency to governorship, national assembly and state assembly seats, opposition candidates have not been finding it easy to campaign as they wish as they are faced with various forms of harassment, suppression and intimidation. Weekend Trust reports that 31 states in the country are under the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) while two of the remaining five opposition governors have been included in the presidential campaign council of the party. Our correspondents recall that within the week, the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) was attacked in Cross Rivers State, while the bid by the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to hold a rally in Sokoto met with stiff opposition and in Edo and Plateau States, the billboards of major opposition candidates were pulled down. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgement, nullified the emergence of the former Senate President, David Mark, Rauf Aregbesola and others as national officers of the ADC. item.title: The night of January 15, 1966 – General Paul Tarfa
item.description: General Paul Chabiri Tarfa joined the Nigerian Army as a cadet in 1962 and remained there until 1988, serving for 26 years. In that span of time he held many positions – Assistant Adjutant General, Provost Marshal, Commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy. He also served as the governor of the old Oyo State in 1978. After retirement, he served as the managing director of the Nigerian Railways and also had a brief assignment to reorganise the Nigerian Customs. At 85, he is still busy as the chairman of the North-East Development Commission. He shared his experiences with Weekend Trust. I would like to start with your home, Garkida, which I think is a well-known centre for missionary and western education. Do you think the fact that you were born there has had a very huge impact on how your life turned out? Of course, Garkida is one of the old places in the North where missionaries set up and gave us good footing in education. I must say that in those days we were privileged to have been among the early people in the North, especially the North-East, to be introduced to western education. Habiba: The woman behind ‘Jaiz Bank’s N100m investment scheme’ 2027: Opposition’s battle for space That is not to say that Islamic education was not there, but surely, we were lucky to have the missionaries as far back as March 1923, to be precise. You can imagine that it is well over 100 years now. We have benefitted. We had early education and were introduced to secondary school. We had good medical care, which many of our people in the North were not privileged to have. We went from primary to secondary school, from where we had the advantage of being successfully qualified to get enrolled into the Nigerian Army. I think you went to secondary school in Yola and not Garkida, right? Well, Garkida laid the foundation before going to Yola – provincial secondary school in those days. There were only 12 in the entire North and Yola was one of them. It was from there that I had the opportunity to get into the army. You became a cadet in the army in April 1962, but it didn’t take long before you were taken to Canada, a very strange place for someone coming from this part of the world. Before going there, we were told what it would be. Even before then, in Geography in secondary school, we had known about temperate countries, hot countries and so on, of which Canada was one. So when we got to Canada, we were very well equipped and properly prepared, physically and mentally. Your career in the army took off after you returned to Canada. This was 1963? Yes. We came back in December 1963, received at Kano airport, taken to Kaduna and received by the duty officer, who at that time happened to be a man called Benjamin Adekunle. He was a captain and we were just second lieutenants. The so-called “black scorpion”? He asked: “Who among you is Paul Tarfa?” I said I was the one and he said “congratulations”. item.title: Anambra will deliver over 50% of 2027 votes to Tinubu — Soludo
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has promised to deliver at least 50 percent of the state’s votes to President Bola Tinubu, the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the 2027 general elections. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ The governor made the declaration during the flag off of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) 2027 campaign at Ekwueme Square, Awka. According to him, APGA has no presidential candidate for the 2027 general election and would, therefore, adopt President Tinubu as its preferred candidate. “Today, we adopt the APC presidential candidate, Bola Ahmed Tinubu as our candidate,” he declared, noting that the president had demonstrated love and concern for the Igbo people, particularly the people of Anambra State. The governor recalled that the President had appointed several Anambra indigenes to strategic positions in Lagos State during his tenure as governor. He also recalled that APGA had adopted the presidential candidate of the ruling party in previous elections, noting that the party’s decision to support Tinubu in 2027 was a continuation of that political arrangement that had been in existence. He lamented that Anambra State recorded fewer than 5,000 votes for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, yet the President has continued to address some of the challenges confronting the state and the South-East region. He urged the Anambra electorate to support Tinubu in the 2027 election, arguing that doing so would give the state and the South-East a stronger opportunity to engage with the Federal Government and negotiate for their development. “We need to vote for him in order to sit with the government at the centre and negotiate for the development of the South-East and Anambra State”, he declared. A fair assessment requires us to examine the immediate challenges confronting the economy and the long-term benefits expected from the reforms. Nigeria’s economy was bleeding, and stopping that haemorrhage was necessary to give the country a chance of recovery. Ending fuel subsidy addressed an avenue for corruption and the unsustainable drain on public resources. NELFUND had disbursed over N300 billion to over 1.5m students across 319 tertiary institutions as at October 2026. The cost of food, transportation, housing, healthcare and other essentials continues to put enormous pressure on households. The President’s case for another term should not rest solely on the courage to introduce reforms. item.title: Kwara 2027: Omokanye takes NNPP campaign to Edu, vows rural transformation
item.description: The Kwara State gubernatorial campaign train of the New Nigeria Peoples Party-NNPP led by its governorship candidate, Prince Adetoyese Omokanye, has moved to Tsaragi and Lafiagi in Edu Local Government Area, where the campaign received warm reception from traditional rulers, religious leaders, party members, community stakeholders, youths and women. The campaign visit, which attracted a broad spectrum of community representatives and political stakeholders, provided an opportunity for the NNPP governorship candidate to present his vision for rural development, economic empowerment and improved social infrastructure, while engaging residents on the challenges confronting their communities. item.title: US offers $20m reward for info on ‘Iran’s nuclear program’: CENTCOM
item.description: Washington is offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear program, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war. Read Also: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks after Trump election rout A State Department program, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X. The program was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests. In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges. It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward. Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear program. “If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. “If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.” But the president also said Iran – which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war – is eager to end the conflict. “We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said. Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting. And on Tuesday Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue. Earlier this week Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. item.title: Trump: Lesson for Nigeria, by Stephanie Shaakaa
item.description: Donald Trump wanted the November 3 midterm elections to be about him. He said so repeatedly, urging Americans to vote as though his name were on the ballot. He wanted a Republican victory to demonstrate that his presidency still commanded popular support and that his influence over American politics remained firmly intact. Well, Americans took him seriously. Perhaps more seriously than he expected. Democrats have won control of both chambers of the United States Congress, delivering a major electoral setback to Trump and his Republican Party. Yet, as the results became clear, Trump reached for an explanation that seemed to contradict his own campaign message. In a post on his Truth Social platform, he declared: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” The irony is difficult to miss. He had spent weeks asking Americans to treat the election as a verdict on his presidency. When the verdict went against him, he suddenly appeared to be distancing himself from it. He wanted the political benefits of making the election about him without accepting the consequences when voters delivered an unfavourable answer. For readers in Nigeria, it is worth explaining what America calls midterm elections and why they matter. In the United States, a president is elected for a four-year term, but congressional elections take place every two years. This means that halfway into a president’s tenure, Americans return to the polls to elect members of the legislature. These elections are called midterms because they take place in the middle of a presidential term. Congress has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, while senators serve six-year terms, with approximately one-third of the 100 Senate seats contested every two years. Midterm elections do not determine who becomes president. The sitting president remains in office. Instead, voters decide which party controls Congress and, by extension, how much support or opposition the president will face in the legislature This gives Americans an opportunity to express satisfaction or dissatisfaction with a president’s performance without waiting another four years. They can strengthen the president’s party in Congress or hand control to the opposition, making it considerably more difficult for the president to advance his legislative agenda. That is precisely what has happened to Trump. American presidents often benefit from what is known as the coattail effect. When a president is popular, candidates from the same party can benefit from that popularity. His political strength becomes an advantage for others seeking elective office. But when a president becomes unpopular, the effect can work in reverse. Candidates associated with his administration may find themselves paying the price for public dissatisfaction with his leadership. In political terms, this is sometimes described as negative or reverse coattails. Tru

item.title: From open pavilion to nation of orderlies: Is Zik’s ‘fear-free’ Nigeria still possible?
item.description: .What a 1960 inauguration says about fear in today’s corridors of power By Omeiza Ajayi Nearly 66 years after Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was sworn in as Nigeria’s first African Governor-General, the footage of that day – which has again recently gone viral – raises an uncomfortable question: why did a leader who held the highest office in the land need no retinue of security details standing behind him, while today every minister, and even some local government supervisors, cannot move without a swarm of details? The inauguration took place on November 16, 1960, at Tafawa Balewa Square, barely six weeks after independence. It was also Zik’s 56th birthday. The narrator of the newsreel set the scene plainly. “At the steps of the pavilion stand the Prime Minister and the Lord Chief Justice, symbolising the people and the law, on what is surely one of the most important occasions in the history of the country.” No armed escort looms in the frame. No aide hovers at the shoulder of the man the crowd was chanting for. “Zik! Zik!” rang around the square as he arrived, and the vast stands, in the narrator’s words, were “hushed.” Today the picture is reversed. In Abuja and in the state capitals, orderlies trail ministers into halls and offices. The situation is so bad that some security personnel actually enter into very enclosed spaces or rooms with their AK47 rifles in clear breach of security protocol. At the local government level, some unelected supervisory councillors have been known to move with armed vigilance team members or hunters, sometimes to intimidate the very people they were appointed to serve. The easy explanation is insecurity, and it is not a false flag. Banditry, kidnapping and insurgency have made parts of the country dangerous, and no leader can be faulted for fearing for his life. But the leaders of other nations also face threats. Behind the American president or a British prime minister stand trained protective officers, assigned to a defined danger. They do not crowd every public official, from the cabinet room to the ward office, with men whose chief duty is to announce importance. It is not uncommon in Nigeria to see security details standing and blocking a television camera. That leaves the harder question. Are Nigeria’s leaders afraid of the general state of the country, or have they become afraid of their own people? Zik, standing in the open that November morning, appeared to have settled that question for himself. He began his address with these words: “It is with humility, mingled with joy, that I thank this grand concourse of patriots and friends of Nigeria for congregating here today on the occasion of my inauguration as the first African Governor General and Commander-in-Chief of the Federation of Nigeria.” He titled the speech “Respect for Human Dignity,” and he made no secret of what he feared for Nigeria. item.title: Daddy Showkey: Vanguard Award will be the biggest of my lifetime
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe & Benjamin Njoku Chief John Odafe Asiemo, 57, popularly known as Daddy Showkey, is a household name in Nigerian music scene. He is the creator of ‘Galala’ music, which sound helped define Nigeria’s street music in the 90s. Speaking with ululation after being presented with the letter of nomination, on Tuesday at his Lagos residence, he said: “They say a prophet is not recognised by his own people. But I am a prophet who is being recognised by the people who built me. This is the greatest awards I have ever received in my life because it is coming from Vanguard. This is Vanguard, and I cherish it a lot. “Apart from that, Vanguard played a big role in pushing me to the limelight. “So, a recognition award coming from Vanguard, I must cherish it. After my secondary education, I hit the streets. From childhood, I had made up my mind to follow music. At 13, in 1983, I started following Danladi Bako of NTA. I remember saying one day while walking past Vanguard ‘this newspaper will one day write about me.’ It came to pass when Ogbonnaya wrote about me for the first time. The second was Smart Irewudo, a former Champion Newspaper reporter, now based in the United States. Before I started recording, during the June 12 crisis, I led Ajegunle boys who blocked roads and extorted money from motorists. Smart took my picture and published it in the Daily Champion. item.title: Police rescue 10 stolen children in Abia
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Abia State Police Command has arrested suspects linked to the October 17 attack on Uratta Divisional Police Headquarters, rescued 10 stolen children and recovered 15 firearms and 30 stolen vehicles in a major security crackdown across the state. The Command also disclosed that it arrested 109 suspects, comprising 89 males and 20 females, in connection with 211 criminal cases recorded between September 11, 2026 and November 6, 2026. Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, who disclosed this on Friday while presenting the Command’s operational scorecard, said the arrests followed intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies. On the Uratta police station attack, Afolabi said investigations had led to the arrest of some of the suspected attackers, with one of them allegedly confessing to leading the gang that carried out the assault. He said investigations were ongoing to track down other accomplices and establish the full circumstances surrounding the attack. In a related security operation, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit raided a location at Ubakala, Umuahia South Local Government Area, on October 25, arresting a suspect identified as Osita. The police reportedly recovered two locally fabricated guns, 16 live cartridges and four expended cartridges from the suspect. Another suspect, 30-year-old suspect, was subsequently arrested for allegedly supplying ammunition illegally. Both suspects have been charged to court, according to the CP. On child trafficking, Afolabi said police operatives rescued 10 children during the period under review and reunited them with their families. He specifically disclosed that two suspects, including a 38-year-old , were arrested on October 11 over the alleged stealing of two children, seven-year-old Chiamaka Chikeze and nine-month-old Goodluck Chikeze. The children were reportedly recovered and handed back to their parents, while the suspects were charged to court. The police boss also announced the arrest of a five-man vehicle theft syndicate, aged 43, and 40. A Toyota Corolla with registration number ROU 9338J was recovered from the suspects, who have also been charged to court. In another operation, two suspected cultists, aged 27, and 25, were arrested on October 31 for allegedly dispossessing students of Abia State University, Uturu, of their mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint. A locally fabricated firearm was recovered from them. The CP said one of the suspects had confessed to belonging to the Black Axe Confraternity, adding that efforts were ongoing to apprehend other members of the gang.
